study.title: YouTube comments on the Amanpour and Company Khlaaf segment
study.artefact_title: "What Really Happened When OpenAI Bots Escaped a Cybersecurity Test?" (Amanpour and Company, PBS)
study.central_claim: The real story of the OpenAI agent-swarm incident is corporate negligence and hype, not a machine going rogue.
study.capture_method: Complete yt-dlp export (--write-comments --extractor-args "youtube:max_comments=999999,all,999999,all"), full threading, like counts and timestamps. Second capture; the first (13 September) underpins the published article's headline numbers, which this recode targets rather than supersedes.

spot_check.note: Random 40-comment sample (with parent text for replies) checked against the codebook on stance, frame, format reaction and emotion; 40/40 agreed, no corrections.

study.coders: Claude (claude-sonnet-5), two parallel coders of 161 comments each

changelog.note: Second-capture coding run behind the published article (322 comments, two parallel coders, 14 frames plus other). Not archived as a row-level file; described only in the article's method section and the project findings note.

Row-level recode from the raw yt-dlp export, since coded_full.json was never archived. Frame list redrafted from the article's own documented frames and quotes, aimed at reproducing the published figures rather than an independent fresh read. Reproduces the published article's structural counts exactly (322 rows, 232/90 top-level/reply split, 1,048 likes, 237 authors) and lands close on most headline figures (disagree's like share exact at 1.6%; hype-or-staged, regulation and hostile-dismissal within a point of the published shares). Runs higher on agree share (72.7% vs 67.7% published) and lower on mixed (8.6% vs 14.3%), and under-counts explicit messenger-credential mentions (3 of 322 here vs 7 published) despite a targeted check against the article's own quoted examples. Ben Matthews spot-checked a random 40-comment sample and approved proceeding, 40/40.

study.notes: Unlike the Soares, Cotra and METR recodes in this series, the published article and findings note for this study are already accurate and current (verified against each other line by line before this recode began); this dataset is a best-effort reconstruction of the missing row-level file, not a correction. Where this recode's shares diverge from the published article (see changelog v2), that is expected drift from a redrafted codebook and should not be read as the published figures being wrong.

codebook.central_claim: The real story of the OpenAI agent-swarm incident is corporate negligence and hype, not a machine going rogue.
codebook.stance_note: agree = accepts Khlaaf's reframing that the real story is corporate negligence, not a rogue machine; disagree = rejects this and defends the rogue/dangerous-AI framing, including from the AI-safety side; mixed = accepts part, rejects or reframes part.
codebook.coder_instructions: For replies, parent-comment text is supplied as context only; code the reply itself, not its parent. Comments with no readable position (jokes, tangents, single reactions) are stance na. When a comment fits two frames, pick the one it leads with. This codebook was redrafted from the second capture (16 September 2026); the original 13 September codebook was not archived, so frame-level figures are a best-effort reconstruction aimed at the published article's own numbers, not an independent fresh read.
